To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a focal lesion of spinal cord in an in vitro preparation results in secondary damage to spinal locomotor networks below, but not at the lesion site.
a focal injury in an in vitro spinal cord model results in a loss of locomotor networks within 24 h.
a focal lesion of the spinal cord causes early changes in the locomotor network of the segments below the lesion, which may have important consequences for the long‐term function of these networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the early stages of secondary damage in a model that may be useful to investigate pharmacological interventions to limit the extent of injury.
the mechanisms of secondary damage following a focal lesion and the dynamics of early locomotor system dysfunction.
the development of an in vitro model to investigate the mechanisms underlying secondary damage following spinal cord injury.
